verdict.rationale: Orama's pricing page calls Orama JS 'The open-source search library', and the docs refer to an 'Orama Open Source' edition. A public GitHub repository (github.com/oramasearch/orama) is cited, so the core library's source appears readable. The evidence never names the specific license, and nothing shows the Cloud product (context server, MCP server, REST APIs) is source-available, so complete coverage is not shown. missing for 10: explicit license name/terms (e.g., an OSI license file citation), evidence on whether Cloud/on-prem components are open source, independent corroboration of the licensing.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The open-source search library. Add fast, relevant search to your own application at no cost.
so you can easily migrate your projects from **Orama Cloud** to **Orama Open Source** and vice-versa
